title: Latency SLA–aware kernel composer with prefill telemetry
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Problem: The runtime currently picks kernels based on per-op microbenchmarks and a simple cost model that underperforms tail latency for mixed prefill/decode workloads. For requests with substantial prefill tokens the optimal allocation of attention and matmul kernels differs from short-decode-only paths. Goal: Create a low-risk heuristic composer that assembles a per-request kernel plan using live prefill telemetry and an SLA-aware latency budget to reduce 95th/99th percentile latency regressions while preserving average throughput and cost targets. The approach should be incremental and rollback-friendly so we can iterate safely on production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency reduces by >=8% on mixed prefill:decode benchmark vs baseline
No more than 3% regression in average throughput on steady-state batched workloads
Feature can be toggled per-customer and per-route via runtime flags
Has end-to-end canary rollout plan with automatic fallback on latency regressions
implementation_plan: Spike: collect prefill telemetry (prefill length distribution, cache hit ratios, observed attention kernel latencies) from a 1% traffic mirror
Design a lightweight per-request latency budget generator that splits target SLO across prefill and decode phases
Implement composer module that selects kernels from existing catalog given budget, seq-len, and occupancy constraints
Integrate composer into request admission path behind feature flag and run closed-canary using runtime routing
Add metrics and alerts (per-route kernel mix, budget exceed events, tail latency by kernel combo)
Iterate on heuristics for mixed-length flows and document rollback criteria
